trials.riddle: Reveal everything standing in your current room.
trials.teaches: ls lists the contents of a room (directory).

trials.riddle: Reveal even the HIDDEN passages here (names that begin with a dot).
trials.teaches: ls -a shows hidden entries whose names start with a dot.

trials.riddle: Cast the spell that tells you exactly where you stand.

trials.teaches: cd <room> walks you into another directory.

trials.riddle: Climb back to the room you came from.
Read the entire scroll lying in this room.
trials.hint: conCATenate the scroll to your screen.
trials.teaches: cat <file> prints a file's full contents.

trials.riddle: Peek at only the FIRST lines of the scroll.
trials.teaches: head shows the first lines of a file.

trials.riddle: Glimpse only the LAST lines of the scroll.
trials.teaches: tail shows the last lines of a file.

trials.riddle: Hunt the scroll for the word 'amulet'.
trials.teaches: grep finds lines matching a pattern inside a file.

trials.riddle: Count how many lines the scroll holds.
trials.teaches: wc -l counts the lines in a file.

trials.hint: One word — it 'touches' a file into being.

trials.riddle: Summon your inventory by echoing the $I treasure-rune.
trials.teaches: echo prints text; $I holds your inventory.

trials.riddle: Run the 'treasure' encounter waiting in this room.
trials.teaches: ./<script> runs an executable in the current room.

trials.riddle: Draw the map of the whole dungeon.
trials.hint: One short word — or the branching 'tree'.
trials.teaches: map / tree reveal the dungeon's layout.

cards.q: Sort names.txt in reverse order.
cards.why: -r reverses the order.

cards.q: Sort numbers.txt numerically, so 10 comes after 9.
cards.why: -n compares numbers, not text.

cards.q: Sort names.txt and drop duplicate lines, in one command.
cards.why: -u keeps one copy of each line.

cards.q: Rank the lines of counts.txt from the largest number to the smallest.
cards.why: -n numeric plus -r reverse: biggest first.

cards.q: Collapse repeated lines of piped input and count each one.
cards.why: uniq -c prefixes each line with its count.

cards.q: Print only the lines of list.txt that are repeated.
cards.why: -d shows duplicated lines only.

cards.q: From data.csv, keep only the 2nd comma-separated field.
cards.why: -d, sets the delimiter, -f2 picks field 2.

cards.q: Keep characters 1 to 3 of every line of codes.txt.
cards.why: -c selects character positions.

cards.q: Turn every lowercase letter of piped input into uppercase.
cards.why: tr maps SET1 onto SET2 character by character.

cards.q: Delete every digit from piped input.
cards.why: -d deletes the characters in SET1.

cards.q: Replace every 'cat' with 'dog' on every line of pets.txt.
cards.why: s/old/new/ substitutes; the trailing g means every match on a line.

cards.q: Reverse the characters of each line of word.txt.
cards.why: rev mirrors each line.

cards.q: Make a backup copy of config.txt named config.txt.bak.
cards.why: cp SOURCE DEST keeps the original.

cards.q: Rename draft.txt to final.txt.
cards.why: Renaming is moving to a new name.

cards.q: Delete the file junk.tmp.
cards.why: rm is permanent: look before you delete.

cards.q: Make deploy.sh executable.
cards.why: +x adds the execute permission.

cards.q: Take the execute permission away from deploy.sh.
cards.why: -x removes it.

cards.q: Set the variable COLOR to blue.
cards.why: No spaces around the =.

cards.q: Add 5 to the number held in MANA.
cards.why: Inside let, names are numbers: no $ needed.

cards.q: Make ll a shortcut for ls -F.
cards.why: Quote the command so its space stays inside.

cards.q: Print every exported variable.
cards.why: env lists NAME=value pairs.

cards.q: Page through big.log one screen at a time.
cards.why: Space pages forward, b back, q quits.

cards.q: Print poem.txt with its lines numbered.
cards.why: nl numbers lines.

cards.q: Ask what kind of thing 'mystery' is before opening it.
cards.why: file identifies text, directories and programs.

cards.q: Draw the directory tree under where you stand.
cards.why: tree shows the whole structure at once.

cards.q: Load the definitions in setup.sh into the current shell.
cards.why: source runs a file in THIS shell, so its variables stay.

cards.q: Open the manual page for grep.
cards.why: man is the built-in documentation.

cards.q: List the command lines you typed recently.
cards.why: history remembers every line.

cards.q: Print the value of the variable HOME.
cards.why: $NAME expands to the variable's value.

List files and directories in current location
List with type indicators: * = executable, / = directory, @ = link
List ALL files including hidden (.), with permissions and details
List with human-readable file sizes
Move up one directory level
Go back to previous directory
Find files/directories by name pattern
Find only files
Find only directories
Search for pattern in all files recursively
Show command history
Check your inventory
Check your health points
Read area documentation

cards.why: cd <room> walks you into another directory.

cards.q: Glimpse only the LAST lines of the scroll.
cards.why: tail shows the last lines of a file.

cards.q: Hunt the scroll for the word 'amulet'.
cards.why: grep finds lines matching a pattern inside a file.

cards.q: Count how many lines the scroll holds.
cards.why: wc -l counts the lines in a file.

cards.q: Conjure a brand-new room called 'workshop'.
cards.why: mkdir creates a new directory (room).

cards.q: Forge an empty artifact named 'torch'.
cards.why: touch creates an empty file.

cards.why: echo prints text; $I holds your inventory.
